reviews.rationale: Low: explicit title-purpose closure; function, not chapter number, decides the seam.

reviews.rationale: Low: speaker and full speech frame are explicit; no ontology is decided.

reviews.rationale: Medium: the sequence is linked rhetorically, though its sub-admonitions are partly detachable.

reviews.rationale: Low: marked beatitude and praise movement.

reviews.rationale: The promises and neighbor duties remain adjacent within one parental instruction, so the selected child requires its 3:21-35 parent for retrieval.

reviews.rationale: The list is rhetorically complete, yet it remains the ethical application within the larger my-son address that opened at 3:21.

reviews.rationale: Low: explicit audience, tradition frame, and closing promise.

reviews.rationale: Low: vocative and sustained two-path contrast.

reviews.rationale: Low: renewed vocative and coordinated body imagery.

reviews.rationale: T467 chapter-coincident hold: a complete warning-counterinstruction arc is visible, but inner movement seams are plausible.

reviews.rationale: Low: explicit condition and rescue closure.

reviews.rationale: Low: named addressee and completed observation/application.

reviews.rationale: Shared body and discord vocabulary link the two neighboring forms, but the explicit numerical reset supplies the stronger internal seam.

reviews.rationale: The catalogue is independently coherent as a numbered wisdom form without turning its shared vocabulary into a claim about source history.

reviews.rationale: Low: vocative, sustained danger, and consequence closure.

reviews.rationale: T467 chapter-coincident hold: the frame-narrative-appeal arc is positive evidence, while the embedded narrative is a plausible smaller unit.

reviews.rationale: Low: speaker and public summons are marked.

reviews.rationale: Medium: this remains part of the larger Wisdom speech.

reviews.rationale: Medium: translation and ontology pressures are substantial; the decision is literary scope only.

reviews.rationale: Low: conclusion formula and terminal antithesis.

reviews.rationale: Low: scene, emissaries, and quoted invitation.

reviews.rationale: Medium: speaker attribution and exact relation to the invitations are ambiguous.

reviews.rationale: Low: new character, parallel invitation, and terminal disclosure.

reviews.rationale: High seam uncertainty: catchword and role links are real but do not authorize collection history.

reviews.rationale: High: aphoristic catchword clustering is contestable; retain named-collection parent.
reviews.support: Blessing and wicked-mouth violence recur at both edges; righteous memory and wise reception occupy the center.

reviews.rationale: High: verses 15-16 broaden to wealth/wages within the chain.
reviews.support: Hatred/love opens; lips, slander, concealment, speech abundance, and righteous lips/tongue repeatedly govern the sequence.

reviews.rationale: High: thematic rather than formal closure.
reviews.support: YHWH's blessing opens; wicked desire/fear and storm passing contrast with the righteous person's durable hope, days, and unshaken land status.
reviews.counterevidence: A chapter-end seam would interrupt the mouth/YHWH transition continued in the next unit.

reviews.rationale: The explicit speech envelope closes at 10:32; chapter numbering is not the reason for the seam.
reviews.support: Mouth, tongue, and lips repeat across both bicola, contrasting produced wisdom and acceptable speech with a perverse tongue and perverse speech.
reviews.counterevidence: The rejected 10:31-11:1 bridge depends on generalized moral cadence, while 11:1 changes topic and imagery from speech organs to false and just measures.

reviews.rationale: The thematic and lexical integrity chain is coherent but retains medium confidence because aphoristic cluster boundaries remain contestable.
reviews.support: False balance and just weight open an integrity evaluation that continues through pride and humility, integrity guidance, wealth failure, righteousness, and deliverance before mouth-based neighbor harm begins at 11:9.
reviews.counterevidence: Starting at 11:2 would detach the balance aphorism from its following integrity sequence, while attaching 11:1 backward would merge distinct speech and measurement forms.

reviews.rationale: High: surety may begin a new sequence.
reviews.support: Mouth-based destruction/deliverance opens; city rejoicing, gossip/trust, counsel, and surety all concern social stability.
reviews.counterevidence: Splitting city/counsel from speech would lose their shared communal-order function.

reviews.rationale: High: loose anthology adjacency and translation pressure.
reviews.support: Honor/wealth introduces gendered character contrasts; kindness/cruelty, deceptive wages, steadfast righteousness, and the ring-in-swine image all evaluate character and outcome.
reviews.counterevidence: Isolating 11:22 as a memorable image would detach its character-evaluation role.

reviews.rationale: High: fruit vocabulary supports but does not prove the scope.
reviews.support: Desire/outcome opens; giving and withholding lead to blessing, trust, flourishing, fruit, and recompense in the land.
reviews.counterevidence: Ending before 11:31 would weaken the repeated outcome/recompense closure.

reviews.rationale: High: thematic cluster has no explicit superscription.
reviews.support: Love of correction opens; good/wicked favor, rooted righteousness, household shame/crown, and the house-standing contrast converge on stability.
reviews.counterevidence: Chapter-sized or one-verse chunks would miss the rooted/house-standing movement.

reviews.rationale: High: compassion vocabulary interrupts a tight work chain.
reviews.support: Praise/contempt opens; lowly productive work contrasts with pretension, cruelty, empty pursuits, and wicked desire, closing with righteous-root fruit.
reviews.counterevidence: Separating work and root images would understate the productivity motif.

reviews.rationale: Medium-high: 12:15-16 adds counsel/anger but remains speech-response related.
reviews.support: Lip transgression opens; mouth fruit, fool/wise counsel, rash/healing words, truthful/lying lips, deceit, and prudent concealment dominate.
reviews.counterevidence: One proverb per unit would erase the sustained speech vocabulary.

reviews.rationale: T467 chapter-coincident risk: local life-path closure exists, but 13:1 may continue instruction contrasts.
reviews.support: Diligent versus lazy hand opens; anxious heart and good word, neighbor guidance, sloth/diligence, and the righteousness path culminate in life.
reviews.counterevidence: The chapter boundary is retained only because the life-path line provides a positive collection cadence.

reviews.rationale: High: son formula may merely be another independent aphorism.
reviews.support: Wise son/discipline opens; mouth fruit and guarding lead into appetite/diligence, lying, and righteousness guarding the way.
reviews.counterevidence: A seam at 13:3 would detach guarded mouth from guarded conduct.

reviews.rationale: High: light and pride sayings weaken thematic unity.
reviews.support: Rich/poor reversal opens; wealth as ransom, righteous light, pride contention, and diminishing versus gathered wealth share possession/outcome concerns.
reviews.counterevidence: One-verse units would obscure the repeated wealth/outcome vocabulary.

reviews.rationale: Medium-high: the desire inclusio is positive, while internal sayings remain aphoristic.
reviews.support: Deferred versus fulfilled desire opens; command/fear, wise teaching, prudence, messenger, correction, and fulfilled desire close the inclusio.
reviews.counterevidence: Splitting before 13:19 would lose the repeated desire-fulfilled frame.

reviews.rationale: High: household/result linkage is broader than a formal seam.
reviews.support: Walking with wise/fools opens; good/wicked outcomes move through inheritance and provision to parental discipline and righteous/wicked appetite.
reviews.counterevidence: Isolating child-discipline verses would detach them from household provision and outcome.

reviews.rationale: High: several adjacent topics make the outer seam provisional.
reviews.support: Wise/foolish woman building/demolishing a house opens; walking, mouth, ox/work, witness, fool, and guilt all test whether conduct builds or corrupts communal life.
reviews.counterevidence: A chapter-sized unit lacks specificity, while one-verse units erase house/work/witness interaction.

reviews.rationale: High: strong local echoes but no explicit boundary formula.
reviews.support: The heart's private bitterness/joy opens; house/tent outcomes, way-seeming-right, laughter/grief, backslider, prudent belief, anger, simplicity, and evil bowing form inner-state-to-outcome contrasts.
reviews.counterevidence: Isolating 14:12 would detach the deceptive-way maxim from its emotional and social consequence sequence.

reviews.rationale: High: neighbor and fear motifs are linked by consequence rather than syntax.
reviews.support: Poor/rich neighbor treatment opens; mercy and labor lead through wisdom/witness to fear-of-YHWH confidence and fountain-of-life closure.
reviews.counterevidence: Breaking before the fear-of-YHWH pair would remove the refuge/life culmination.

reviews.rationale: T467 chapter-coincident risk: royal/public-order frame is plausible but not certain.
reviews.support: A king's populous glory opens; patience/envy, oppression of poor, national righteousness, and servant/king favor close as public-order evaluations.
reviews.counterevidence: A raw chapter seam is rejected; the royal frame and national/king closure provide the positive rationale.

reviews.rationale: Medium-high: 15:3 and 15:6 broaden the field.
reviews.support: Gentle/grievous answer opens; tongue, YHWH's watching eyes, healing tongue, correction, and wise lips dominate to 15:7.
reviews.counterevidence: Each speech proverb alone would lose the answer/tongue/lips chain.

reviews.rationale: High: multiple mini-clusters may justify smaller units.

reviews.rationale: High: catchword linkage is modest.

reviews.rationale: T467 chapter-coincident risk: a wisdom-instruction cadence supports the seam, but the named collection continues.
reviews.support: YHWH tears down/establishes opens; thought/word, unjust gain, listening, correction, fear of YHWH, and humility-before-honor provide a collection cadence.

reviews.rationale: Medium: exact start may include 15:33 as a thematic preface.

reviews.counterevidence: One-verse segmentation would erase the dense human-plan/YHWH-response chain.

reviews.rationale: Low-medium: concentrated king vocabulary provides a strong cluster.

reviews.rationale: High: path and speech motifs overlap but do not fix an exact seam.

reviews.rationale: T467 chapter-coincident risk: strong opening echo and closing providential cadence coexist with loose internal adjacency.

reviews.rationale: High: verses 3-5 broaden beyond household.

reviews.rationale: High: the gift sayings may constitute a separate pair.

reviews.rationale: High: adjacency is more evident than formal unity.

reviews.rationale: T467 chapter-coincident risk: the child/fool frame is positive but the interior is mixed.

reviews.rationale: Medium-high: 18:4 offers a positive wisdom-word counterpoint.
reviews.support: Self-separation and rejected wisdom open; fool mouth/lips repeatedly produce strife and ruin, ending with gossip entering inward parts.
reviews.counterevidence: One proverb per unit would erase the mouth/lips/words escalation.

reviews.rationale: High: a compact interpretive cluster with no explicit formula.

reviews.rationale: Medium-high: gift and dispute verses broaden but remain communicative/social.

reviews.counterevidence: Isolating 18:21 would detach the famous tongue saying from the hearing/dispute/speech sequence.

reviews.rationale: T467 chapter-coincident risk: relational vocabulary links three sayings, but the cluster is weak.

reviews.rationale: High: witness sayings interrupt the poverty/friend chain.

reviews.counterevidence: Separating wealth/friend sayings from poor-person frame would lose the social reversal.

reviews.rationale: High: multiple plausible subclusters.
reviews.support: Gaining wisdom opens; lying witness, fool luxury, discretion, king's wrath/favor, foolish son, wife, and deep sleep/sloth form governance of self and house.
reviews.counterevidence: A royal-only split at 19:12 would be too small and detach rule from household governance analogies.

reviews.rationale: High: linked by instruction and consequence more than catchword.

reviews.counterevidence: Isolating child discipline would detach it from the broader teachability/counsel frame.

reviews.rationale: T467 chapter-coincident risk: resistance-to-instruction theme is plausible but not formal.

reviews.counterevidence: The chapter seam is not sufficient; the closing judgment line supplies a positive cadence.

reviews.rationale: High: exact cohesion is modest.
reviews.support: Wine's mockery opens; king's terror and avoiding strife move to sloth, deep counsel, claimed loyalty, and the righteous person's intergenerational integrity.
reviews.counterevidence: Single sayings would hide the sober self-governance/integrity movement.

reviews.rationale: High: sleep proverb is a clear interruption.

reviews.counterevidence: Separating measure and buyer sayings would weaken the evaluation-of-claims motif.

reviews.rationale: High: thematic synthesis remains debatable.
reviews.support: Precious knowledge-lips open; surety pledge, deceptive food, counsel for plans/war, gossip, parent-cursing, and hastily gained inheritance evaluate unreliable gains and commitments.
reviews.counterevidence: One-verse chunks would lose the speech/commitment/gain sequence.

reviews.rationale: T467 chapter-coincident risk: several judgment images cohere, but the unit is composite.

reviews.rationale: High: royal opening may stand alone.
reviews.support: King's heart in YHWH's hand opens; YHWH weighs hearts, justice outranks sacrifice, pride, diligent plans, lying treasure, robbery, and crooked/clean ways extend evaluated conduct.
reviews.counterevidence: Splitting after the royal saying would isolate the governing evaluation frame.

reviews.rationale: Medium: intervening aphorisms are diverse but the repeated better-than frame is strong.

reviews.counterevidence: Separating the two contentious-wife sayings would lose their envelope function.

reviews.rationale: T467 chapter-coincident risk: a strong terminal saying does not prove the preceding cluster's exact start.

reviews.counterevidence: The final victory line provides cadence; nevertheless a cross-chapter continuation remains possible.

reviews.rationale: High: famous-verse extraction is avoided, but the thematic seam is uncertain.
reviews.support: Good name versus riches opens; rich/poor maker, prudent refuge, humility/fear reward, crooked thorns, and training a child share durable path/reputation outcomes.
reviews.counterevidence: Isolating 22:6 would detach the path-training saying from adjacent path/outcome contrasts.

reviews.rationale: Medium-high: inner cohesion is loose, but the endpoint is a strong named-collection seam.
reviews.support: Rich/borrower power opens; sowing injustice, generous eye, scoffer removal, purity/speech, YHWH guarding knowledge, sluggard excuse, dangerous mouth, discipline, and oppression close immediately before a new wise-sayings address.

reviews.rationale: Low: explicit collection/addressee prologue.
reviews.support: 'Incline your ear and hear the words of the wise' opens direct instruction; keeping them, trust, repeated writing, and reliable return-speech state the collection's purpose.
reviews.counterevidence: 22:17 alone would detach the invitation from its purpose and assurance.

reviews.rationale: This compact prohibition-and-divine-reversal form is complete but must retain the larger 22:17-24:22 collection parent.
reviews.support: The paired prohibitions against robbing the poor and crushing the afflicted at the gate receive their matching reason: YHWH will plead their cause and despoil the despoiler.
reviews.counterevidence: Joining 22:22-23 to the anger warning would combine two instructions merely because they are consecutive in the words-of-the-wise sequence.

reviews.rationale: The cause-and-consequence syntax favors this pair while leaving its placement within the wider instructional collection non-authoritative.
reviews.support: A negative companion command names the angry person, and the purpose clause closes with the danger of learning that path and ensnaring oneself.
reviews.counterevidence: Extending through 22:27 would conflate character imitation with the separately framed surety warning and its bed-removal consequence.

reviews.rationale: The pair is a complete warning; retrieval must not imply a general legal ruling beyond its received wisdom context.
reviews.support: The prohibition against hand pledges and debt surety is answered immediately by the rhetorical threat that the debtor bed will be taken away.
reviews.counterevidence: Merging the pledge warning with 22:24-25 would erase the change from dangerous friendship to a discrete financial-social practice.

reviews.rationale: Its aphoristic closure is clear; mandatory parent and sibling hydration prevents isolated legal or historical overreading.
reviews.support: The single prohibition against moving an ancient boundary marker names both the protected object and the ancestral act that established it before a new topic begins.
reviews.counterevidence: Joining 22:28 to surety or skilled service would hide its self-contained land-boundary function, though a naked single verse would lose collection context.

reviews.rationale: The saying is complete as a bicola, but it must surface with the named wise-sayings parent and nearby siblings.
reviews.support: The rhetorical observation of a person skilled in work resolves in the contrast between standing before kings and standing before obscure people.
reviews.counterevidence: Attaching 22:29 to the boundary-stone warning would create a thematic cluster without a shared speaker, syntax, or repeated lexical frame.

reviews.rationale: The scene and imperative chain close at 23:3, while the wider wise-sayings parent remains necessary context.
reviews.support: A when-clause places the learner at a ruler table; observe, restrain the throat, and distrust deceptive delicacies complete one high-stakes appetite instruction.
reviews.counterevidence: Joining through 23:5 would combine court-table self-control with the next instruction against exhausting oneself to acquire wealth.

reviews.rationale: Imperative and image form a closed warning, although its economic language remains translation-sensitive evidence only.
reviews.support: The command not to wear oneself out for riches is followed by a rhetorical glance and the eagle-wing image in which wealth vanishes.
reviews.counterevidence: Absorbing 23:4-5 into the ruler-table scene would treat two distinct appetite objects as one instruction without a continuing situation.

reviews.rationale: The guest-host reversal is coherent, while the precise Hebrew description of the host is not used to select a preferred translation.
reviews.support: The evil-eyed host opens a meal scene; deceptive hospitality, inward calculation, and the guest vomiting the morsel and losing praise resolve the warning.
reviews.counterevidence: Extending to 23:9 would merge a narrated hospitality trap with a direct prohibition against speaking wisdom to a fool.

reviews.rationale: The one-verse form is bounded but is never retrieved without parent and sibling hydration because its application is easy to overgeneralize.
reviews.support: The direct command not to speak within a fool hearing supplies its own reason: that audience will despise the prudence of the words.
reviews.counterevidence: Joining this aphorism to the stingy-host episode would confuse a speech-audience rule with the prior meal scene.

reviews.rationale: The protected parties and Redeemer consequence close the pair, without converting wisdom language into a legal code.
